source_inventory.title: Induced path distance on a round unit sphere
source_inventory.edition: Self-contained geometric supplement, 2026-11-16; expanded exposition of the exact 2026-11-09 contract
source_inventory.kind: one universal distance identity with four definitions, five assumption paragraphs, six proof sections and three boundary paragraphs
source_inventory.attribution_scope: Original exposition of a classical round-sphere distance formula; no claim of novelty or attribution to a primary textbook theorem.
source_inventory.statement_scope: Every endpoint pair on the actual positive-dimensional round unit sphere, including coincident and antipodal pairs.

reconstructed_source_statement: Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space and n a natural number with n > 0 and dim_R E = n + 1. Let S = {z in E : ||z|| = 1}, with its sphere smooth structure and literal inclusion iota : S -> E. Assign a tangent vector v at z the induced length ||D iota_z(v)||_E. For each x,y in S, take the infimum over all C^1 paths gamma : [0,1] -> S with gamma(0)=x and gamma(1)=y of their induced speed length. As an extended nonnegative quantity this equals the nonnegative embedding of theta = arccos(<x,y>_R), where 0 <= theta <= pi. The theorem establishes finiteness and does not replace the inherited chord metric.

definitions.body: S is the norm-one subtype of E; iota sends a sphere point to that very ambient vector.
definitions.required_identity: Actual unit sphere and literal inclusion, not an abstract equivalent sphere or arbitrary embedding.

definitions.body: At z in S, evaluate the actual differential D iota_z on the tangent vector v, then take its ambient norm.
definitions.required_identity: The norm belongs after the inclusion differential. A default norm of chart coordinates is not the defined speed. The scalar norm law is a consequence of linearity, not an extra hypothesis.

definitions.body: For an endpoint-constrained C^1 path on [0,1], integrate its induced speed on that interval; the formal length uses a nonnegative extended lower integral.
definitions.required_identity: Interior/within derivatives are reconciled almost everywhere. An ordinary integral can be substituted only after continuity/measurability, integrability and the nonnegative embedding comparison have been justified.

definitions.body: Extended-nonnegative infimum of these lengths over every admissible endpoint-constrained C^1 unit-interval path.
definitions.required_identity: No minimizing path is an input; the constructed arc proves a finite candidate exists. Equality to an angle requires the explicit finite embedding into the extended codomain.

order: finite dimension and natural n with n > 0 and dim_R E = n + 1
infimum binds every endpoint-constrained C^1 path gamma on [0,1]
indispensable_geometry: Positive sphere dimension permits a unit vector orthogonal to x, including at antipodal endpoints.
The sphere manifold model is selected using the rank equality.
The ambient structure is real, so the inner product, real arccos and real tangent scalar law agree.
scope_of_auxiliary_quantifiers: The lower bound applies to every admissible path, not just the constructed arc.
For each such path, regularization uses every real a with 0 < a < 1, then a tends to 1 from below.
The great-circle frame u is chosen after the endpoints and need not be unique.
Differential speed identifications need only hold in the interior/almost everywhere for the integral; the distance conclusion holds for all endpoint pairs.
not_assumed: An already supplied path or geodesic
Unit-speed parametrization of an arbitrary path
A derivative bound or length estimate
An auxiliary measure or arbitrary tangent norm as theorem data
Existence of a global Riemannian bundle metric instance
conditions_and_quantifiers.constant_dependencies: The unit radius fixes the coefficient: there is no unspecified constant or dependence on a path, endpoint separation or dimension. The only universal upper angle bound is pi.

substantive_moves: Compose an admissible manifold path with the literal inclusion to obtain an ambient curve f.
Apply the manifold chain rule to identify D iota_gamma(t)(gamma velocity) with the ambient velocity.
Use interior agreement of within-interval derivatives and disregard the two endpoints only under the interval length measure.
proof_topology.output: Induced speed agrees almost everywhere with ambient speed on [0,1].
review_obligations: Check that the differentiated path and inclusion are the actual objects from the distance definition.
Check the manifold/ambient derivative comparison on the interval interior and the precise null-set/measure statement.

substantive_moves: Differentiate ||f(t)||^2=1 to get <f(t),f prime(t)>=0.
For c(t)=<x,f(t)>, rewrite c prime=<x-c f,f prime>.
Use ||x||=||f||=1 and c=<x,f> to obtain ||x-c f||^2=1-c^2.
Apply Cauchy-Schwarz and nonnegativity of 1-c^2.
proof_topology.output: |c prime(t)| <= sqrt(1-c(t)^2) ||f prime(t)|| on the relevant interior.
review_obligations: The x used in c is the first endpoint, so c(0)=1.
No unit-speed assumption is permitted for an arbitrary path.

substantive_moves: Fix 0<a<1; |c|<=1 keeps a c strictly inside (-1,1).
Differentiate arccos(a c); its derivative is -a c prime/sqrt(1-a^2 c^2).
Bound this signed derivative by a sqrt(1-c^2)/sqrt(1-a^2 c^2) times speed, then by speed since a^2(1-c^2)<=1-a^2 c^2 and the denominator is positive.
Use C^1 regularity and compactness to integrate, giving arccos(a<x,y>)-arccos(a)<=integral speed.
Let a tend to 1 from below and use continuity of arccos and arccos(1)=0.
proof_topology.output: theta <= ordinary integral_0^1 ||f prime(t)|| dt for every admissible path.
review_obligations: The limit is of endpoint expressions with a fixed right-hand side; no unproved dominated convergence or derivative continuity at arccos singular endpoints is needed.
FTC/integration must support within-interval regularity and one-sided endpoint behavior.

substantive_moves: Set theta=arccos<x,y>; Cauchy-Schwarz gives theta in [0,pi].
Set r=y-<x,y>x; prove r orthogonal to x and ||r||=sin(theta), using nonnegativity of sine on [0,pi].
When r is nonzero, put u=r/||r||.
When r=0, choose a unit u in x-perp, using dim E>=2; unit endpoints then give y=x or y=-x, and the common endpoint formula still holds.
proof_topology.output: A unit u orthogonal to x with y=cos(theta)x+sin(theta)u, including theta=0 and theta=pi.
review_obligations: The zero residual case cannot be silently excluded.
The chosen frame has no global smoothness or uniqueness requirement.

substantive_moves: Construct ambient f_star(t)=cos(t)x+sin(t)u and use the orthonormal frame to show it stays on the sphere.
Lift the curve smoothly to the actual sphere and differentiate it; its ambient speed is one.
On [0,theta], verify the endpoints and length integral_0^theta 1=theta.
Transfer to the unit-interval distance definition using a justified reparametrization/path comparison and the scalar norm law from linearity of the inclusion differential.
proof_topology.output: d_S(x,y) <= the nonnegative embedding of theta.
review_obligations: For theta=0 the unit-interval representative is constant; the nondegenerate unit-interval speed is theta, not one.
A path comparison that assumes strictly positive interval length needs an explicit zero-length branch.
Differentiability of the sphere lift and the local norm law must be proved, not imported as extra hypotheses.

substantive_moves: Show the ambient within-interval speed of an arbitrary C^1 path is continuous on the compact interval and hence integrable.
Use almost-everywhere integrand equality and the nonnegative integral/lower-integral comparison to identify formal path length with the finite embedding of the ordinary speed integral.
Promote the lower bound for each admissible path to the infimum lower bound.
Combine it with the explicit upper arc, obtaining extended-nonnegative equality and therefore finiteness.
proof_topology.output: d_S(x,y)=ofReal(arccos<x,y>) for all sphere endpoint pairs.
review_obligations: Ensure the actual lower-integral domain and measure match the ordinary interval integral.
Check the infimum indexing includes exactly all admissible paths; existence follows from the arc, not a hidden global connectivity assumption.

must_remain_visible_in_reader: Actual inclusion-induced speed and retained chord metric
Arccos regularization, including its reason at +/-1
Antipodal/zero-residual frame branch using positive dimension
Zero-length endpoint case and unit-interval comparison
Extended nonnegative codomain and finiteness conclusion

natural_mathematics_assessment.source_argument_status: The six-section argument is mathematically coherent at its stated level. No extra theorem hypothesis is needed by the supplied argument. The operational bridges listed per section remain checks for the later compiler/source/reader review; this source-only phase does not certify their implementation.
notation_precision: The displayed real angle must be understood through the nonnegative embedding when compared with the formal extended distance.
C^1 on a closed interval requires the stated within-interval interpretation or an appropriate extension; endpoint derivative values alone do not affect length.
The unit-speed statement applies to f_star in angle time on [0,theta]; it is not the general unit-interval parametrized speed.

boundary_inventory: The chord metric is retained and differs from the induced length distance (antipodal values 2 and pi).
The n=0 sphere is excluded essentially for the all-pairs statement.
No general manifold geodesic existence, global Riemannian instance, stochastic result, transport estimate or textbook chapter completion is claimed.
Spherical transport is only a possible consumer; no actual dependency edge to such a theorem is established by this source.
